nodes.rationale: Strava upload polls at most once every 2s up to 30 times since Strava processes uploads asynchronously.

nodes.label: brouter.de rate limit (403 retry later)
nodes.rationale: Client retries with delay; requests per generation cut from ~24 to ~8 via radius calibration; own BRouter instance mandatory for thousands of users

nodes.label: Dynamic search zone (calibrated radius)
nodes.rationale: Initial radius distance/(2pi x detour factor 1.25 bike, 1.3 run), corrected from distance actually obtained; first direction calibrates, zone grows for 60-100 km

nodes.label: Loop scoring and rejection rules
nodes.rationale: Score = 3 x distance gap + 2 x doubled share + (1 - way quality) + optional relief; reject >20% off, >35% doubled, >60% similar; explain instead of inventing a route

nodes.label: Relief preference replaces exact elevation target
nodes.norm_label: relief preference replaces exact elevation target
nodes.rationale: D+ still computed from engine elevations worldwide, guides ranking instead of being an exact target

nodes.label: 300 m start/end privacy mask
nodes.rationale: Hides home location on traces shown to others; plus per-activity visibility and private profile

nodes.label: Shared pure-Python business code
nodes.rationale: Business logic at repo root is shared between the app and the server so it is written once

nodes.label: Five-step Strava GPX import guide with app screenshots
nodes.norm_label: five-step strava gpx import guide with app screenshots

nodes.label: Loopy home page
nodes.rationale: Two distinct GPX exports never confused: itinerary (no time) vs activity (timestamped). Loopy invents no duration or speed.

nodes.label: Importer sur Strava guide page
nodes.rationale: Manual GPX import on strava.com while direct Strava upload is not configured; the Strava mobile app cannot import files.

nodes.rationale: App that traces a real loop around the user's position anywhere in the world, for cycling or running, then tracks the outing and exports/sends it

nodes.label: APK build (buildozer.spec)
nodes.rationale: Adds INTERNET and ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE, openssl and certifi for up-to-date HTTPS, and .brf profiles; server/site not embedded

nodes.label: Works without account or server
nodes.rationale: Generation, outing, history and GPX stay on the phone; the account only adds sync, community and Strava

nodes.label: Loopy website README
nodes.rationale: Served by serveur/app.py on same origin as the API: same account as the app; no build, no npm

nodes.label: No-build site (HTML/CSS/ES modules)
nodes.rationale: Served by same server: same origin, simple cookies, nothing to compile

nodes.label: Single account system (scrypt, hashed tokens)
nodes.rationale: App uses Bearer token, site uses HttpOnly SameSite=Lax cookie with anti-CSRF header; one account system for both

nodes.label: Accessibility and reduced motion
nodes.rationale: prefers-reduced-motion respected, visible keyboard focus, sufficient contrast light and dark, text equivalent for each chart

nodes.label: Known limits (in-memory rate limiter, plaintext Strava tokens, uncapped tile cache)
nodes.norm_label: known limits (in-memory rate limiter, plaintext strava tokens, uncapped tile cache)

nodes.label: Server environment variables
nodes.rationale: No secret in code; values come from environment or a git-ignored .env

nodes.label: SMTP settings
nodes.rationale: Without SMTP the reset link is logged: fine for dev, not production

nodes.label: Strava application setup and upload flow
nodes.norm_label: strava application setup and upload flow
nodes.rationale: Callback /api/strava/retour, scopes activity:write,activity:read; single player mode until capacity raised; POST /api/v3/uploads then poll GET /uploads/:id

nodes.label: Production deployment (HTTPS proxy, single worker)
nodes.rationale: Single uvicorn worker because rate limiter is in memory; HTTPS needed for site geolocation; back up LOOPY_DONNEES with sqlite3 .backup

nodes.label: correctMisplacedViaPoints
nodes.rationale: Avoids dead-end out-and-backs to touch a via point

nodes.label: GraphHopper hosted API (rejected)
nodes.rationale: Free tier non-commercial, no flexible mode so no custom model or round trip; remains a self-hosted option

nodes.label: Local OSM graph via Overpass (rejected)
nodes.rationale: Public Overpass saturated (39 s then at capacity) and forbids automated traffic

nodes.label: OpenRouteService (alternative)
nodes.rationale: Native round trips limited to 100 km, fixed profiles; untested, good alternative

nodes.label: Self-hosted BRouter instance
nodes.rationale: Public brouter.de throttles active clients; own instance on port 17777 with 5 degree .rd5 segment tiles; profiles sent via POST /brouter/profile

nodes.label: FastAPI + SQLite (WAL) server choice
nodes.rationale: Same language as the app so boucles.py, gpx.py, geo.py are shared; single DB file easy to back up

nodes.label: Legacy core.py Dijkstra on data.db graph
nodes.norm_label: legacy core.py dijkstra on data.db graph
nodes.rationale: Replaced: whole graph loaded at startup, seconds of load and memory proportional to zone, impossible to extend to the world

nodes.label: BRouter choice
nodes.rationale: Client-sent scriptable profiles, real OSM tags per segment (surface with confidence), no API key, 0.3 s response with elevation; production just swaps the URL to an own instance

nodes.label: Geographic limit (5 km around Pessac)
nodes.rationale: data.db was prepared once by prepare_data.py (osmnx) for a 5 km circle around Pessac with walk network only, embedded in the APK; max distance 20 km, no bike profile

nodes.label: New loop generation requires network
nodes.rationale: Computation is on the routing engine; saved loops, outings, history and cached map remain offline

nodes.label: Activité page
nodes.rationale: Hides the trace when shorter than 2 points so the start is not revealed (privacy).
